correctness.rationale: For fixed \(r>1\), \(C>0\) and real \(d,e\), conditioning on the high-variance maximum yields an exact finite-n probability integral with density \((1-y/n)^{n-1}\). The Gaussian Mills ratio and inverse quantile admit uniform expansions on \([L^{-3},L^3]\), while excluded regions have total probability \(O(L^{-3})\). The parameter-dependent exponent correction follows from multiplication of independent second-order factors and is integrated with bounded Taylor remainders \(O((\log L)^2/L^2)\). The signs and optimized coefficients follow by \(H>0\). The bundled finite integral verifier passed 36 assertions for three distinct variance ratios, but finite checks are not used to infer the theorem.

originality.rationale: The mathematically closest full text, Zhang–Miao–Mao (arXiv:2605.21155), Theorem 1, establishes the first-order nondegenerate Gaussian two-group winner limit at the critical sample-size scale. Its Sections 2–4 give no displayed or implied coefficient for the signed \((\log\log n)/(\log n)\) finite-size probability bias or the unique two-term correction. Gasull–Jolis–Utzet (arXiv:1308.5541) refine marginal normal maxima, while Davydov–Rotar provide general argmaximum first-order limits; neither inspected statement dominates this probability correction. Published record searches did not identify the same correction. This supports a provisional originality assessment, not independent priority certification.

value.rationale: The motivating heteroscedastic maximum problem naturally asks how to choose group sample sizes to obtain a prescribed group-winning probability. The previously known critical power/log scaling controls only the limit. The new signed bias quantifies the systematic error in the standard leading sample-size rule and gives a unique two-term adjustment that cancels all errors through order \(1/\log n\). This is a nontrivial distributional refinement requiring explicit integration of normal-tail second-order terms; it is not a renaming or a table recomputation.
